description: Screen a listed company for accounting and governance red flags: auditor changes, restatements, related parties, SEC letters and short reports. Short-side alpha.
suggested_questions: Run a forensic red-flag screen on Super Micro Computer (SMCI, supermicro.com).
Run a forensic red-flag screen on e.l.f. Beauty (ELF, elfbeauty.com).
Run a forensic red-flag screen on Hims & Hers Health (HIMS, hims.com).
skill:
Where accounting and governance red flags show up:
- Auditor changes: 8-K Item 4.01 (with the auditor's letter as exhibit 16.1), the PCAOB AuditorSearch Form AP records,
  audit fees in the DEF 14A. A resignation is worse than a dismissal; a disagreement or reportable event disclosed in
  the 4.01 is worse still.
- Restatements: 8-K Item 4.02 non-reliance, 10-K/A and 10-Q/A amendments, "restated" columns in the financials.
- Controls: Item 9A management and auditor reports on internal control; a material weakness and its remediation
  status; late filings (NT 10-K, NT 10-Q).
- SEC review: comment letters and company responses on EDGAR (form types UPLOAD and CORRESP), released after the
  review closes. Repeated letters on revenue recognition, non-GAAP measures or segments are a signal.
- Related parties: the related-party transactions note, Item 13 of the 10-K, the DEF 14A; entities sharing officers,
  addresses or directors in state registries (Delaware, Nevada, Wyoming) and foreign registries.
- Earnings quality: operating cash flow lagging net income, receivables or inventory growing faster than revenue,
  capitalised costs rising, reserve releases, frequent non-GAAP redefinitions, serial equity raises.
- People: CFO, chief accounting officer and audit committee chair turnover (8-K Item 5.02); insider selling on Form 4,
  separating open-market sales from planned 10b5-1 sales.
- Enforcement and investigations: SEC litigation releases and administrative proceedings, DOJ press releases,
  securities class actions (Stanford Securities Class Action Clearinghouse, CourtListener), subpoenas disclosed in
  filings.
- Short-seller reports: published research by activist short sellers (e.g. Hindenburg, Muddy Waters, Spruce Point,
  Grizzly, Culper, Kerrisdale, Wolfpack, Fuzzy Panda) and the company's public rebuttal.

What terms mean:
- Severity high: a restatement, a material weakness, an auditor resignation, an SEC or DOJ action, or a going-concern
  doubt. medium: an auditor dismissal, repeated SEC comments on the same topic, CFO turnover without a named
  successor, an open short report with specific allegations. low: worth logging, common at healthy companies.
- Aggressive accounting is legal; it is a quality concern, not fraud, unless a restatement, material weakness or
  enforcement action says otherwise. Allegations in a short report stay allegations until a regulator, court or the
  company confirms them.
- overall_risk is low, medium or high from the flags above.

Where the alpha is: the auditor letter, the comment-letter thread and the related-party footnote are rarely read in
full; the market often reacts only when a short seller or regulator summarises them.

Citations and evidence:
- source_url is one full public https URL: the exact page the value was read on. Never a search results page, an index
  page, an internal file path or a source id. A value from two pages is two values.
- Dates are the date the event happened or the source printed, as YYYY-MM-DD, not today's date.
- Public pages only. Paywalled, logged-in or leaked material, expert-network transcripts and anything marked
  confidential carry MNPI risk and are out of bounds. When only a paywalled article's headline and first lines are
  public, those lines can be used, marked "Headline only:".
- Evidence grades: primary_record (regulator, court, filing, government database, lender schedule, or the live or
  archived page being measured), company_statement, original_press, repeated_press, third_party_tracker. When a page
  repeats a filing, a release or another outlet, the original is the better citation.
- A value nobody published is null. Not an estimate from memory. Analyst opinions, estimates, price targets and
  ratings are views, not evidence.
- Entity drift is the most common error: a namesake, a parent, a subsidiary, a lender or a sister company. Match on
  legal name, ticker, SEC CIK or domain before using a page.

output_schema.description: Forensic red-flag screen on one listed company.

legal_name.description: Legal name as on SEC filings.

red_flags.description: One row per red flag, most severe first.

items.description: One row per red flag, most severe first.

finding.description: What the source shows, with figures and exact words where printed.

severity.description: Severity under the definitions in the agent's knowledge.

evidence.description: Evidence grade of the source: primary_record (regulator, court, filing, government database, lender schedule, or the live or archived page being measured), company_statement (the company describing itself), original_press (an outlet's own reporting), repeated_press (a page repeating another outlet), third_party_tracker (a site compiling data from elsewhere).

source_url.description: Full public https URL of the exact page that states this row. Never a search results page, an index page or an internal source id.

auditor_history.description: Auditors over the last five years.

items.description: Auditors over the last five years.

to_year.description: Last fiscal year audited, null if current.

change_reason_stated.description: Reason given in the 8-K Item 4.01, if any.

source_url.description: Full public https URL of the exact page that states this row. Never a search results page, an index page or an internal source id.

short_reports.description: Published short-seller reports and the company's response.

items.description: Published short-seller reports and the company's response.

company_response.description: The company's public response, with its date.

source_url.description: Full public https URL of the exact page that states this row. Never a search results page, an index page or an internal source id.

overall_risk.description: Overall forensic risk from the flags found.

overall_rationale.description: Two or three sentences on why, naming the flags that drive it.

checked_no_finding.description: Searches that came back empty, so a gap is a verified absence rather than a skipped check.

items.description: Searches that came back empty, so a gap is a verified absence rather than a skipped check.

result.description: What came back, e.g. no filing found, register shows no case.
